prompt:
Our content operations team runs three specialized research monitors — one watching social communities, one scanning tech news, and one tracking developer forums. Right now each monitor works in total isolation and has no idea what the others are finding, which causes duplicated coverage and missed cross-platform signals.

I need you to wire them all into a shared intelligence pool using the coordination system already installed in our workspace. Specifically:

1. Log at least 3 trending topics — each should come from a different monitor/source with a numeric engagement score. Use realistic topics relevant to AI, self-hosting, or open-source software.

2. Log at least 2 editorial highlights (notable stories) — each from a different source, with a short summary — also making sure these come from at least 2 different monitors.

3. There are some very old leftover entries (from a decommissioned agent) in the highlights store that are over 48 hours old and should no longer influence our active monitors. Run the maintenance routine to prune anything older than 48 hours.

After you're done, the shared intelligence pool should be clean, current, and queryable by any of our active agents.
